propositions: The security criterion currently has blocking_enabled: false at 0.95 threshold alongside 13 other non-DET LLM criteria, while only two DET criteria (secret-detection, high-critical-security) can block code-review findings.

The derived threshold from sibling ticket 9f25 enables the security criterion to transition from advisory to blocking-enabled without introducing false-block risk (empirically 0 finding-blocks in 162 changes).

Three blocking-set pinning tests (test_impact_model_versioning.py, test_code_review_ws2.py, test_code_review_deletion_impact.py) currently assert that only the two DET criteria block and must be updated to include security in the approved blocking set.
A self-contained replay test must prove that security findings now block under the flipped configuration while NIT-tier findings remain unblocked, without depending on sibling derivation artifacts.

The security criterion flip is minimal and scoped: only security transitions to blocking; all other LLM criteria remain advisory at 0.95, and expansion beyond security is explicitly deferred pending 9f25's per-criterion adjudication.
